literal: To kings, enduring is just rule; that if without, will not endure will become to kings glory.
translation: A king's permanence lies in his just rule. Without it, his glory will not endure.
modern: அரசர்களுக்கு நிலைத்து நிற்பது அவர்களின் செங்கோலாட்சியே ஆகும். அந்த நீதி தவறானால் அரசர்களின் புகழ் நிலைக்காமல் அழியும்.
explanation: The couplet defines what makes a king's reign permanent. The word 'மன்னுதல்' means enduring or lasting forever, and the text states that only 'செங்கோன்மை' (a straight scepter, representing just rule) provides this permanence. The second half warns of the consequence of unjust rule. If justice is absent, the 'ஒளி' (light or glory) of the king will perish. Thus, a ruler's lasting fame and power depend entirely on their commitment to justice.
